composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Runs first. When the 'Idempotency-Key' header repeats a key already seen, short-circuit with a
# 200 replay of the originally created owner (before the duplicate check below would 409); otherwise
# publish the key for RecordIdempotency and continue building.
checkIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckIdempotency
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

# Assign the deterministic householdId (SHA-256 over lastName + postcode). It no longer drives
# duplicate detection; it is retained for household-size and membership derivations. Owners at the
# same last name and postcode are the same household.
assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureUniqueIdentity

# The single duplicate block: reject a second owner whose identityKey (SHA-256 over normalized
# telephone + lower-case email + soundex of the last name) matches an existing one with 409, unless
# the request set 'sharesHousehold' to declare it a household member.
ensureUniqueIdentity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureUniqueIdentity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCustomerCode

assignCustomerCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignNamesakeCount

assignNamesakeCount:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureCityCapacity

ensureCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureDailyOwnerLimit

ensureDailyOwnerLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureDailyOwnerLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignPossibleDuplicate

# Soft match: flag an owner whose identityKey differs from an existing one but whose soundex(lastName)
# and postcode match. A declared household member ('sharesHousehold') is never flagged.
assignPossibleDuplicate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignPossibleDuplicate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: recordIdempotency

# Owner is now persisted (id assigned); remember it against the Idempotency-Key (if any) so a repeat
# replays this owner. No-op when the request carried no key.
recordIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RecordIdempotency
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName,
                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: >-
                The stored E.164 'telephone' formatted for humans: the country code, a
                space, then the national digits grouped in threes. So '+61412345678' is
                shown as '+61 412 345 678'. The raw 'telephone' stays in E.164 form.
              type: string
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code formatted '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>', where CITY3
                is the upper-cased first three letters of the city, LAST3 the upper-cased
                first three letters of the last name and NNNN a per-city 4-digit
                zero-padded sequence assigned at creation.
              type: string
              example: 'LON-SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                A single Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits of the
                customerCode.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 4
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A deterministic identifier shared by every owner in the same household: the
                first 12 hex characters of SHA-256 over the normalized last name and postcode.
                Assigned to every owner, so owners at the same last name and postcode share it
                automatically.
              type: string
              example: '3f2a1b0c9d8e'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The single derived key all duplicate detection is expressed through: the
                lower-case hex SHA-256 of the normalized telephone, the email (or empty when
                absent) and the Soundex code of the last name, joined with '|'. A create is
                rejected with 409 only when a new owner's whole identityKey equals an existing
                (non-deleted) owner's.
              type: string
              example: '9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners (as of this owner's creation) that share
                the same first name and last name, compared case-insensitively.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicate:
              title: Possible duplicate
              description: >-
                True when this owner, though not a hard duplicate (its identityKey differs),
                was created sharing an existing owner's Soundex of the last name and postcode;
                otherwise false. Determined at creation.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicateOf:
              title: Possible duplicate of
              description: >-
                The id of the existing owner this owner soft-matched on Soundex of the last
                name and postcode at creation, when 'possibleDuplicate' is true; absent otherwise.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 7
              readOnly: true
            fiscalYear:
              title: Fiscal year
              description: >-
                The owner's fiscal year formatted 'FY<YY>', where YY is the last two digits
                of the fiscal year (starting 1 July) containing the business-day-adjusted
                registrationDate. So a registrationDate of 2026-09-06 falls in the fiscal
                year ending 2027 and yields 'FY27'.
              type: string
              example: 'FY27'
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>', where YY
                is the last two digits of the fiscal year (starting 1 July) containing the
                registrationDate.
              type: string
              example: 'LON-SMI-0007-M27'
              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: >-
                The owner's membership points: starts at 0, plus 2 when an email address
                is present, plus 1 when namesakeCount is 0, plus 2 for a household of 3 or

Done. Here's what I did and why.

## Situation

The repo's **only** test — `AcceptanceTest.coreReturnsUnifiedMemberId` — is the forward-looking spec for the *unimplemented* change (it asserts a `memberId` field exists and `customerCode`/`membershipNumber` are gone). It was already red before I touched anything, and it **cannot go green without implementing the change**, which this task explicitly forbids. The hotspot classes `MemberIds`, `AssignMemberId`, and `Owner.getMemberId/setMemberId` don't exist yet — they're where the change will land.

So I did preparatory restructuring only, keeping every already-passing behavior byte-identical (verified: the response body and audit line are unchanged — `checkDigit:8`, `customerCode:"NSW-16E6609E"`, `membershipNumber:"NSW-16E6609E-M27"`, `fiscalYear:"FY27"`, `locality:"NSW"`). No regression: the same single pre-existing failure remains.

## Where the change's complexity was going to concentrate, and how I relieved it

The upcoming `memberId = <REGION><FY><HASH8><CHK>` gathers pieces that today are **inlined or duplicated**, which is exactly why the direct implementation overloaded `MemberIds`/`AssignMemberId`/`OwnerMapper`. I pulled those pieces into the clean, single-responsibility seams this codebase already favours (`Soundex`, `FiscalYears`, `Households`, … — `final` helpers with a private ctor and an `Owner`-level method):

1. **Extracted the Luhn algorithm** out of `OwnerMapper.checkDigit` into a new `Luhn` helper (`Luhn.checkDigit(String)`). The future `MemberIds.luhn` (the CHK over `<REGION><FY><HASH8>`) becomes a one-line delegation instead of a re-implementation.

2. **De-duplicated `membershipNumber`.** It was copy-pasted verbatim in `OwnerMapper.membershipNumber` and `AuditOwnerCreated`. Now there's a single `CustomerCodes.membershipNumber(Owner)`; both callers delegate. The change removes it from one place.

3. **Made `CustomerCodes` the coherent home for the whole derived-value cluster** its own Javadoc already names ("membership number, its check digit, … hang off" the identity): added `CustomerCodes.checkDigit(Owner)` and exposed `CustomerCodes.hash8(Owner)` (the "same first-8-hex used by the region-and-hash identity" the new format reuses). `OwnerMapper.checkDigit` now delegates too. So the change consolidates region/hash8/checkDigit/membershipNumber into `MemberIds` as **one natural move** rather than untangling them from four call sites.

`OwnerMapper.locality` and `.fiscalYear` were left as-is — they were already thin delegations, and stay thin when the change re-points them at `MemberIds`.

## What I deliberately did **not** do

- No `memberId` field, no `MemberIds`/`AssignMemberId` classes, no schema/OpenAPI/DTO edits, no collision-handling rework — all of that *is* the change.
- Didn't touch `AssignCustomerCode`'s collision loop: memberId's fixed-width format needs different disambiguation than appending `-<n>`, and pre-factoring that would mean guessing the change's design.

**Bottom line:** the sole failing test is the deferred change's acceptance criterion and stays red by design; every existing behavior is preserved exactly. If you'd like, I can now implement the `memberId` change on top of this — it should be a small, clean diff against these seams.
